recordSetsNote: Each entry says what was read and, where it matters, what was not. A source named without that distinction is a citation, not evidence.

recordSets.name: New South Wales civil registration and parish registers
recordSets.body: Including **St James's, Sydney**, where George Lindsay D'Arcy was christened on 5 November 1829.

recordSets.name: Australian newspapers (Trove)
recordSets.body: Death and funeral notices, and the Brisbane press.

recordSets.name: Queensland State Archives, series S36 — Coronial Files
recordSets.body: Item `ITM2736504`, digital representation `DR103140`: the 1902 magisterial inquiry into the death of *William Hartley Sneyd*. **Eighteen images, no text layer, read and transcribed in full from the originals** on 9 September 2026. It supplies four sworn depositions, a post-mortem certificate and a Government Analyst's certificate, and it is **the only record in this archive in which a member of the family speaks about another under oath**.

recordSets.name: National Archives of Australia, series B2455 — First World War service dossiers
recordSets.body:
The thirty-page dossier of *Private Arthur Hartley Sneyd, 5050* (item 8088453) has been **read in full**: attestation, physical description, statement of service, the Army Form B.2090A report of death, and the Kit Store inventory of his effects. The dossier of *L/Cpl Vivian Claude Sneyd, 1696* (item 8087524, 21 pages) has been **partly read** — the Service and Casualty Form and the Statement of Service. A third, *Pte Ernest Vivian William Sneyd, 3891* (item 8087517), was located and **has not been opened**.

For *Sergeant Lindesay Atkinson D'Arcy, 11335*, **no B2455 item could be found** under either spelling. An earlier version of this page said a fourteen-page dossier «is known to exist»; that was an overclaim and is withdrawn. What the search did find is **NAA: J34, C34558**, a Repatriation Commission pension case file of 1937-38 with his widow as beneficiary — not digitised, and not yet read.
recordSets.note: RecordSearch has no stable per-item address that survives a session, so the link opens the search; the item number is in the description above.

recordSets.name: Australian War Memorial, AWM 28 — recommendation files for honours and awards
recordSets.body: The recommendation for the **Bar to the Military Medal** for *1696 L/Cpl Vivian Claud Sneyd, 3rd Australian Field Ambulance*, dated 12 October 1917, endorsed «Awarded» and signed by Lieut-Col. A. Graham Butler — **read and transcribed in full**.

recordSets.name: Australian Red Cross Wounded and Missing Enquiry Bureau files (AWM `1DRL/0428`)
recordSets.body: The twenty-three-page file for *5050 Private Arthur Hartley Sneyd, 9th Battalion*, **read in full**. Six statements taken from men in the hospitals and base depots of France, and two letters from the friend who kept looking for him for thirteen months. **It is hearsay evidence, gathered as such and contradictory on its face**, and it is treated that way here.

recordSets.name: Australian War Memorial — embarkation and nominal rolls
recordSets.body:
Used here for *Sergeant Lindesay Atkinson D'Arcy, 11335* and *Private Arthur Hartley Sneyd, 5050*. The AWM 131 Roll of Honour index card for Sneyd has been read. The **Roll of Honour circular** — the form his family filled in by hand — survives and **has still not been read directly**; one phrase from it reaches this archive at second hand, through the AIF Project's transcription, and is quoted as such: that he «gave up this rank in Egypt in order to get across to France».

AWM's own collection search returned nothing for any query on 9 September 2026 — the Memorial is migrating its records. The documents were reached by direct URL instead.

recordSets.name: Brisbane City Council cemetery registers
recordSets.body: Toowong, Dutton Park, South Brisbane, Nundah, Lutwyche, Mt Thompson.
recordSets.note: This archive's data still cites the council's old host graves.brisbane.qld.gov.au, which no longer resolves at all — it has no DNS record. The search now lives on the council's main site, which is where the link above goes.

recordSets.name: Ireland, Births and Baptisms, 1620–1881 (index, via FamilySearch)
recordSets.body: The christening of Paul Cole Atkinson at Limerick on 9 July 1832, naming *Richard Atkinson* and *Anne*. **RootsIreland itself has not been searched** — it needs a paid account, and a request is drafted.

recordSets.name: Caribbean Birth & Baptism Index 1590–1928
recordSets.body: The christening of Constantine Darcy at **St Michael, Barbados, 18 February 1786**, naming *Robert Darcy* and *Jane*.
recordSets.note: Linked to FamilySearch's *Caribbean, Births and Baptisms, 1590-1928*, whose span matches this row exactly; FindMyPast publishes the same index under the title used here.

recordSets.name: Connolly and Edwards, *Roll of Officers of the Corps of Royal Engineers, 1660–1898*
recordSets.body: R.E. Institute, Chatham, 1898 — entries 203 and 335, for Robert and Constantine D'Arcy. Searched in full via the Internet Archive scan.
recordSets.note: The link reaches the Internet Archive, where this row says the volume was searched. The specific scan is not identified here, so the link is to the archive rather than to the book.

recordSets.name: Kent Burials and Hampshire Marriages (FindMyPast)
recordSets.body: The burial of Robert D'Arcy at St Mary, Chatham, 19 May 1827, and his marriage to **Jean Ward** at Portsea St Mary, 21 June 1779 — the latter re-opened at transcript level on 17 September 2026 to confirm the spouse's surname.

recordSets.name: Australia, Births and Baptisms, 1792–1981
recordSets.body: The christening of George Lindsay Darcy at St James Sydney, 5 November 1829, naming both parents.

recordSets.name: British Newspaper Archive, Family Notices
recordSets.body: The marriage notice of «Captain George d'Arcy», son of «Lieut Colonel d'Arcy», *Salisbury and Winchester Journal*, 23 September 1805.

recordSets.name: Scotland, Civil Registration and Scotland, Marriages (indexes)
recordSets.body: The birth of William Murdoch at St Quivox and Newton, 7 October 1856, naming Francis Murdoch and Marion Watt; and their marriage at Avondale, Lanarkshire, 6 May 1854. **ScotlandsPeople itself, which holds the register images, has not been consulted** — it needs a paid account, and a request is drafted.
recordSets.note: The link opens *Scotland, Civil Registration, 1855-1875, 1881, 1891*. The companion index is *Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910*, FamilySearch collection 1771074.

recordSets.name: FindMyPast — the subscription sets
recordSets.body: Taken out in September 2026 and worked through: **England Births & Baptisms 1538-1975**, which carries a father's first name and yielded 340 baptisms under fifteen spellings of Saniger; **England Marriages 1538-1973**; **England & Wales Deaths 1837-2007**; the **1841, 1851 and 1861 censuses**; and **British Army Lists & Commission Registers 1661-1826**. Every null taken from them names the control that could have disproved it.

recordSets.name: The National Archives — Discovery, by API
recordSets.body: `GET /API/search/records` needs no account, no key and no bot check, and returns JSON. Used to sweep the whole catalogue under fifteen spellings of the surname and nine of its medieval form — 134 and 193 distinct records, across twelve repositories.

private.name: The eulogy for Kenneth Lindsay D'Arcy
private.body: March 2010 — four thousand words in three parts, delivered by Gayle, Ian and Graham D'Arcy. **The single richest source in the archive.**

private.name: A 1970 school photograph
private.body: Pimlico State High School, Townsville, showing Ian D'Arcy — which independently confirms the Townsville decade described in the eulogy.

private.name: The «This Is Your Life» book
private.body: Presented to Ken D'Arcy on his retirement from National Mutual in 1982. Referred to in the eulogy; **not yet located**.
